What happens to frameworks in the agents era? to component libraries? to @shadcn? 

The answer is: we need to drill deeper. Delete the part, optimize, accelerate, automate.

UI SDK is like the x86 instruction set for agents to build new UI components spontaneously. 

Agents are https://t.co/g48EMN54AO

replies.text: Concrete part of the x86 analogy: the same primitives target React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components, with ARIA wiring included. A framework-neutral layer is what lets agent-generated UI stay portable. Visit @nxtday for an insight on what's coming next.

Frameworks do not disappear, they move down a layer. Libraries become primitives agents compose, so the durable work is constraints, accessibility and state, not hand-written JSX. The new bugs will be agents picking the wrong primitive or composing inconsistent states.
If agents write most UI code, do component libraries basically become docs for the model instead of for humans? Feels like the real audience is shifting.
shadcn walked so agents could copy paste at the speed of light
delete the part is a scary sentence if you maintain a component library

Packaged behaviors for focus, keyboard and a11y are what agents get wrong most, so I'm sold on that part. "Zero limitations" is what makes me nervous as a designer. Constraints are how a product stays recognizable. Who decides when a generated component becomes a real one?
I love the presentation video !

Pre-baked component libraries were built for human developers copy-pasting JSX. Agents do not need polished UI kits: they need deterministic primitives, strict design tokens, and rapid visual feedback so they can verify render state without fighting framework abstractions. Giving
My guess is that conventions matter more, not less. Agents do best where there's one obvious way to do things. A framework that removes choices is basically a better prompt.
how is behaviour different than components?
less code fewer bugs
